title: User Result Message
prompt: A TypeScript action returns a small result object for users. Write a function that returns the message field.

explanation.beginner:
Example: userResultMessage({"ok":true,"message":"Saved"}) produces "Saved". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “returns error messages”: input [{"ok":false,"message":"Try again"}] produces "Try again". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “returns error messages”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
